statement: If a straight line be bisected, and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the square on the whole with the added straight line and the square on the added straight line both together are double of the square on the half and of the square described on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line as on one straight line.
heath_proof: For let a straight line AB be bisected at C, and let a straight line BD be added to it in a straight line; I say that the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD. For let CE be drawn from the point C at right angles to AB [I. 11], and let it be made equal to either AC or CB [I. 3]; let EA, EB be joined; through E let EF be drawn parallel to AD, and through D let FD be drawn parallel to CE. [I. 31] Then, since a straight line EF falls on the parallel straight lines EC, FD, the angles CEF, EFD are equal to two right angles; [I. 29]therefore the angles FEB, EFD are less than two right angles. But straight lines produced from angles less than two right angles meet; [I. Post. 5] therefore EB, FD, if produced in the direction B, D, will meet. Let them be produced and meet at G, and let AG be joined. Then, since AC is equal to CE, the angle EAC is also equal to the angle AEC; [I. 5] and the angle at C is right; therefore each of the angles EAC, AEC is half a right angle. [I. 32] For the same reason each of the angles CEB, EBC is also half a right angle; therefore the angle AEB is right. And, since the angle EBC is half a right angle, the angle DBG is also half a right angle. [I. 15] But the angle BDG is also right, for it is equal to the angle DCE, they being alternate; [I. 29] therefore the remaining angle DGB is half a right angle; [I. 32]therefore the angle DGB is equal to the angle DBG, so that the side BD is also equal to the side GD. [I. 6]  Again, since the angle EGF is half a right angle, and the angle at F is right, for it is equal to the opposite angle, the angle at C, [I. 34] the remaining angle FEG is half a right angle; [I. 32] therefore the angle EGF is equal to the angle FEG, so that the side GF is also equal to the side EF. [I. 6] Now, since the square on EC is equal to the square on CA, the squares on EC, CA are double of the square on CA. But the square on EA is equal to the squares on EC, CA; [I. 47] therefore the square on EA is double of the square on AC. [C. N. 1]  Again, since FG is equal to EF, the square on FG is also equal to the square on FE; therefore the squares on GF, FE are double of the square on EF. But the square on EG is equal to the squares on GF, FE; [I. 47] therefore the square on EG is double of the square on EF. And EF is equal to CD; [I. 34] therefore the square on EG is double of the square on CD. But the square on EA was also proved double of the square on AC; therefore the squares on AE, EG are double of the squares on AC, CD. And the square on AG is equal to the squares on AE, EG; [I. 47] therefore the square on AG is double of the squares on AC, CD. But the squares on AD, DG are equal to the square on AG; [I. 47] therefore the squares on AD, DG are double of the squares on AC, CD. And DG is equal to DB; therefore the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD.
ai_proof_text:
2.10
**Statement:** If a straight line be bisected, and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the square on the whole with the added straight line and the square on the added straight line both together are double of the square on the half and of the square described on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line as on one straight line.

**Step 1.** Let the straight line AB be bisected at C, and let the straight line BD be added to it in a straight line, so that A, C, B, D lie in order on one straight line. We must show that the squares on AD and DB together are double of the squares on AC and CD together.

**Step 2.** From the point C draw CE at right angles to AB [1.11], and cut off CE equal to AC, and hence equal to CB, since AC = CB [1.3]. Join EA and EB [P1].

**Step 3.** Through E draw EF parallel to AD, and through D draw FD parallel to CE [1.31]; let these meet at F. Then ECDF is a parallelogram, its opposite sides EF, CD and EC, FD being parallel.

**Step 4.** Since the straight line EF falls upon the parallel straight lines EC and FD, the interior angles on the same side, CEF and EFD, are together equal to two right angles [1.29]. The angle FEB is a part of the angle FEC, so it is less than the angle FEC [CN5]. Therefore the angles FEB and EFD together are less than two right angles.

**Step 5.** Hence EB and FD, if produced in the direction of B and D [P2], will meet on that side [P5]. Let them be produced and meet at G, and join AG [P1].

**Step 6.** Since AC = CE, the angle EAC is equal to the angle AEC [1.5]. The angle ACE is right, so, since the three angles of the triangle ACE are together equal to two right angles [1.32], the remaining angles AEC and EAC together are equal to one right angle [CN3]. Being equal, each of them is half a right angle.

**Step 7.** In the same way, since CE = CB, the angle CEB is equal to the angle CBE [1.5], and the angle ECB is right, so each of the angles CEB and EBC is half a right angle [1.32, CN3]. Therefore the whole angle AEB, being made up of the halves AEC and CEB, is a right angle [CN2].

**Step 8.** The angle EBC is half a right angle; and the angle DBG is equal to the angle EBC, since they are vertical angles formed by the straight lines EG and AD crossing at B [1.15]. Therefore the angle DBG is half a right angle.

**Step 9.** The straight line CD falls upon the parallel straight lines CE and DG, so the alternate angles ECD and BDG are equal [1.29]. The angle ECD is right; therefore the angle BDG is right.

**Step 10.** In the triangle BDG, the angles BDG and DBG together with the angle DGB are equal to two right angles [1.32]; since BDG is right and DBG is half a right angle, the remaining angle DGB is half a right angle [CN3]. Therefore the angle DGB is equal to the angle DBG, and so the side BD is equal to the side GD [1.6].

**Step 11.** Since ECDF is a parallelogram, the angle EFD is equal to the opposite angle ECD [1.34], and so the angle EFD is right; and since G lies on FD produced, the angle EFG is this same right angle. The angle EGF is the same as the angle DGB, so it is half a right angle. Hence in the triangle EFG the remaining angle FEG is half a right angle [1.32, CN3]. Therefore the angle FEG is equal to the angle EGF, and so the side GF is equal to the side EF [1.6].

**Step 12.** Since EC = CA, the square on EC is equal to the square on CA; therefore the squares on EC and CA together are double of the square on CA. But the angle ECA is right, so the square on EA is equal to the squares on EC and CA together [1.47]. Therefore the square on EA is double of the square on AC [CN1].

**Step 13.** Since GF = EF, the square on GF is equal to the square on EF; therefore the squares on GF and FE together are double of the square on EF. But the angle EFG is right, so the square on EG is equal to the squares on GF and FE together [1.47]. Therefore the square on EG is double of the square on EF [CN1]. Also EF is equal to the opposite side CD of the parallelogram ECDF [1.34]; therefore the square on EG is double of the square on CD.

**Step 14.** The angle AEG is right (Step 7), so the square on AG is equal to the squares on AE and EG together [1.47]. By Steps 12 and 13, the squares on AE and EG together are double of the square on AC together with double of the square on CD [CN2]. Therefore the square on AG is double of the squares on AC and CD together [CN1].

**Step 15.** The angle ADG is right (Step 9), so the square on AG is also equal to the squares on AD and DG together [1.47]. But DG = DB (Step 10), so the square on DG is equal to the square on DB, and hence the square on AG is equal to the squares on AD and DB together [CN1].

**Step 16.** Therefore the squares on AD and DB together are equal to the square on AG, which is double of the squares on AC and CD together [CN1]. That is, the square on the whole with the added straight line, AD, together with the square on the added straight line, DB, is double of the square on the half, AC, together with the square on CD, the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line. Q.E.D.
